title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page works out, by hand, the elementary symmetry group of a tube (cylinder) S^1 x I. Coordinates are z in S^1 (or C*) and s a height coordinate on a symmetric interval. In the Teichmüller ('Teichmülleries') context such a tube is the neighbourhood of a simple closed curve on a surface. Its symmetries are the local models for how elements of the extended Teichmüller modular group, or finite subgroups of it, act near an invariant curve.

(1) Top line: the general 'linear' self-maps (z,s) -> (eps z exp(2 i pi a s), eps' s), with eps, eps' in mu (roots of unity; here effectively ±1) and a in Q.
- These are rotations composed with fractional twists of rational amount a, possibly flipping the two ends.
- An equivalent form is ((z exp 2 i pi a s)^{(-1)^nu}, eps s), allowing complex conjugation z -> z^{-1} on the circle factor.
- Grothendieck identifies the resulting group as D_infty x mu: the twist together with an inverting involution generates the infinite dihedral group, and mu is the group of rotations.
- The encircled cases (eps = 1; eps = 1, eps' = -1) single out the pure twist and the end-swapping case. The sketches show a tube crossed by a vertical axis, i.e. a half-turn about an axis perpendicular to the core, and a twisted line, i.e. a Dehn twist.

(2) Named generators:
- sigma_1(z,s) = (z^{-1}, s): reflection of the circle factor.
- sigma_2(z,s) = (z, -s): exchange of the ends.
- a(z,s) = (-z, -s).
- theta(z,s) = (z exp 2 i pi s, s): the twist.

(3) Boxed relations:
- a^2 = sigma_1^2 = sigma_2^2 = 1, with sigma_1, sigma_2, a pairwise commuting.
- Each of sigma_1, sigma_2, a conjugates theta to theta^{-1}.
- The right-hand column contains the explicit verifications:
  - sigma_1 theta sigma_1 = (z^{-1} exp 2 i pi s, s) -> (z exp -2 i pi s, s);
  - sigma_2 theta sigma_2 gives (z exp -2 i pi s, -s) -> (z exp -2 i pi s, s);
  - a theta a gives (-z exp -2 i pi s, -s) -> (z exp -2 i pi s, s).
- So the group generated is Z (twists) ⋊ (Z/2)^3, where each of the three involutions inverts theta.
- Consequently a sigma_2 = (z -> -z), the rotation by pi, centralises theta. This recovers the D_infty x mu description.
- The final line 'a, alpha, beta, theta' suggests renaming the generators for later use.

Purpose: to have explicit local normal forms and relations for the stabiliser of a curve, including orientation-reversing elements and fractional twists. This would serve the description of discrete or finite subgroups and of the 'Lego' gluing of the Teichmüller tower.
errors: All three conjugation computations and the commutation relations check out.

Implicit domain issue. For theta to be a twist fixing both boundary circles while sigma_2 (s -> -s) preserves the domain, s must range over a symmetric interval. On [-1/2, 1/2], theta rotates the boundaries by pi rather than fixing them. On [-1, 1], theta is the square of the standard Dehn twist. So the normalisation is only correct up to the rotation by pi, which is harmless for the relations.
Notation clash: 'a' denotes both the rational twist coefficient a in Q and the involution a(z,s) = (-z, -s).

The box omits the fact, implied by the relations, that the rotation a·sigma_2 commutes with theta. The full group is the product of D_infty with the rotation group, not just the list of relations given.

ideas.what: Symmetry group of an annulus/tube up to twists: Dehn twist theta inverted by reflections and by the end-swap, giving D_infty x mu
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of a simple closed curve in the extended mapping class group (local structure); infinite dihedral group generated by a Dehn twist and an orientation-reversing involution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dehn, Nielsen (classical); standard in mapping class group theory (Birman, Ivanov)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and finite subgroups, but not these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Local models (z,s) -> (eps z exp(2 i pi a s), eps' s), a in Q, for periodic maps near an invariant curve
ideas.modern_name: Fractional Dehn twists / screw numbers of periodic homeomorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Nielsen (1937, screw numbers); later Gilman; fractional Dehn twist coefficients (Honda–Kazez–Matić)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine scratch computations of the symmetry group of a tube (Dehn twist plus involutions, D_infty x mu, fractional rational twists), all classical. They are useful only as evidence of Grothendieck working on local models for finite or discrete subgroups of the extended Teichmüller groups.
transcription_corrections: The struck-out symbol before theta looks like a cancelled 'g'/'β' rather than a clear β.
The relation after the box should read 'a σ_1 = σ_1 a' (written as 'aσ_1 = σ_1 a' at the box edge).
In the right column, one line reads 'z exp −2iπs, +s' (with a plus sign), an intermediate step of the σ_2 conjugation.
Top-right: 'ε, ε' ∈ μ' and 'a ∈ Q'. The exponent in the second line is (−1)^ν.
